doc.title: Directive on Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion

clauses.clause: This directive takes effect on April 1, 2020.
This directive replaces the Treasury Board’s Employment Equity Policy dated July 1, 1999.
This directive is issued pursuant to the same authorities indicated in section 2 of the Policy on People Management.
The objectives indicated in section 3 of the Policy on People Management apply to this directive.

The expected results of this directive are as follows: An equitable, diverse and inclusive workplace where no person is denied employment opportunities or benefits for reasons unrelated to ability or job requirements;Management demonstrates effective leadership by promoting and contributing to employment equity, diversity and inclusion in the workplace; andOrganizational policies and practices respect and promote equity, diversity and inclusion.
The roles of other government organizations in relation to this directive are described in section 5 of the Policy on People Management.
This directive applies to the persons employed and organizations listed in section 6 of the Policy on People Management.

Legislation
Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
Canadian Human Rights Act
Canadian Multiculturalism Act
Employment Equity Act
Employment Equity Regulations
Public Service Employment Act

Related policy instruments
Policy on People Management
Directive on Duty to Accommodate
For interpretation of any aspect of this directive, contact Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat Public Enquiries.

appendix.title: Appendix: Mandatory Procedures for Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion

clauses.clause: These procedures take effect on April 1, 2020.

In conjunction with the Policy on People Management and the Directive on Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, these procedures replace the following Treasury Board policy instrument:
Employment Equity Policy (July 1, 1999)
These procedures provide details on the requirements set out in subsection 4.1 of the Directive on Employment Equity, Diversity and Inclusion.

Mandatory procedures are as follows: When conducting a workforce self‑identification survey, the senior official designated by the deputy head must: Respect the requirements of the Employment Equity Regulations in developing and administering workforce self‑identification questionnaires;Consult with bargaining agents and other employee representatives throughout the process and on the results;Communicate to all employees the purpose and importance of self‑identification;Disseminate self‑identification questionnaires in accessible formats to all employees;Request that all employees return a completed form, whether or not they identify themselves as members of one or more employment equity designated groups;Develop and implement an effective strategy to assess the outcome of the workforce self‑identification questionnaire; andEnsure that information gathered for the purposes of self‑identification is kept confidential and safeguarded appropriately, in accordance with the Employment Equity Regulations.In order to maintain up‑to‑date workforce survey results, the senior official designated by the deputy head must provide a workforce self‑identification questionnaire to persons employed: When they begin or change employment;Who wish to change information previously submitted; orWho otherwise request it.When conducting a workforce analysis, the senior official designated by the deputy head must respect the process prescribed in the Employment Equity Regulations; andWhen completing an employment systems review, the senior official designated by the deputy head must respect the process prescribed in the Employment Equity Regulations.
